messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#6412 HIGH latency spike on hosted-runtime-us-east-1 (p99 > 3s)
pagerduty-bot: Incident triggered for service=hosted-runtime-us-east-1 priority=high — escalation to on-call.
sasha: acked, reading graphs now :eyes:
sasha: p99 jumped to ~5s across the router tier and tails off at the runtime side, looks very short (90s) but loud
dmitri: ack — I'm checking autoscale and recent deploys. no active deploys in the last 30m AFAICT
kevin: i'm seeing increased kernel context switches on a subset of hosts, maybe noisy neighbor on the shared pool? pulling host metrics
infra-ci: synthetic canary checks failing briefly: 2026-03-10T22:14:03Z -> 2026-03-10T22:15:45Z (responses > 3s)
sasha: quick mitigation—temporarily diverting new low-priority traffic to dedicated pool, adding weight to dedicated routing policy
sasha: command I'm running: ```rctrl route set-weight --pool=dedicated-us-east-1 --weight=+15 --reason="latency spike diversion"```
dmitri: confirmed scale-up event started for dedicated pool, +2 instances provisioned
maya: i can hop in for the handoff in 10 mins if you need to walk through anything
sasha: thanks, Maya — I'm going to keep monitoring for a couple minutes then handoff if it stays clear
kevin: host-level telemetry shows one GPU host with very high NVML stall times, cooling on that node also spiked in infra metrics, migrating workloads off it now
dmitri: rolling workloads: ```ssh infra@gpu-node-14 'drain-node && reroute-kv --node gpu-node-14'```
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Alert acknowledged by sasha (oncall)
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty update: alert auto-resolved (no escalation) — duration 2m 3s
sasha: looks like the routing diversion + drain cleared the tail. p99 back to ~200ms
kevin: node 14 has IO wait anomaly, likely underlying host issue, flagged for postmortem with infra team
maya: no customer-facing 5xx spikes in logs, only elevated latency for short window. rolling summary: ~0.18% of requests >3s during spike, no customer errors reported in last 30m
dmitri: double-checked metrics: traffic distribution shows heavy prefix cache misses during the window — KV cache miss rate spiked x3, might explain tail latency
sasha: good catch — could be cache eviction churn + noisy host. we'll add action items
kevin: I'm adding a temporary suppress rule for alerts triggered by a single host's NVML spike so we don't page for single-host flaps: ```alerts update hosted-runtime-us-east-1 --suppress-if-host-count=1 --cooldown=120s```
sasha: Agree with suppression but keep PD for p99>5s across >=3 hosts. Need to avoid masking real incidents.
maya: handoff: i'm oncall for the next 4 hours, i'll watch the graphs, sasha passing to me now :raised_hands:
sasha: handing off — summary: brief p99 spike ~5s for ~90s, caused by NVML/IO issue on gpu-node-14 + KV-cache miss amplification. mitigation: divert low-priority to dedicated pool, drain node-14. auto-resolved after reroute. next steps in thread.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: incident cleared by system (auto-resolved).
dmitri: follow-ups: (1) infra to QA host replacement for gpu-node-14, (2) add KV warmup on instance spin-up to reduce cold miss waves, (3) tune alert suppression to require 2-host correlation or sustained 120s window.
kevin: filed infra ticket INFRA-8792 for host replacement + thermal logs attached
sasha: I'll open a short post-incident note with graphs and timeline, tagging infra and runtime teams.
maya: tiny tweak for alerts: also add a cooldown for synthetic canaries so brief platform noise doesn't wake everyone at 2am. propose cooldown 180s with alert if synthetic fails >2 consecutive checks.
sasha: +1. Action: sasha will write the note, kevin will own INFRA-8792, dmitri will prototype KV warmup script, maya will update alert policy.
incident-bot: thread closed (no active PD escalation).
sasha: nice quick loop, thanks all :thumbsup:
